components.purpose: The cEOS contract as loadable Agent Skills: orient, story-executor, epic-verifier, adversarial-cases, risk-gate, rust-kernel-guard, evidence-packet. Written here, reviewed here, drift-checked by scripts/check_agent_skills.py.

decision.rationale: Authored in this repository under E24. Carries no code and no credentials; a skill is prompt text the agent may load.

components.purpose: PreToolUse guard refusing a hand-edit to a generated document at the moment it is attempted. Fails open on anything it cannot parse.

decision.rationale: Authored here, executes only this repository's own shell script, and the CI drift check remains the authority regardless of whether it runs.

components.purpose: Given one defect, find its variants across the codebase. Automates the lesson of the E00 review history: close the class, not the reported case.

decision.rationale: Trail of Bits is a named security vendor with a public track record. Ships one skill, no hooks, no MCP server: prompt content only.

components.purpose: Rust security review with a worker/judge pipeline, including a false-positive judge. The highest-value component for this project: review throughput is bounded by rounds, and filtering false positives buys more than another reviewer would.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust. Ships three subagents and no hooks or MCP servers, so it can read and reason but cannot install anything or reach the network on its own.

components.purpose: Security-focused review of a diff, with an adversarial-modeler subagent. Directly relevant to the Python-to-Rust migration, where every change is a differential change.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust; prompt and subagents only.

components.purpose: Mutation-testing campaigns. The mechanical answer to the question the verifier asks by hand: would these tests have failed against the pre-fix code? E25-S06 depends on this technique.
Property-based tests. Most of the eleven falsification axes are properties rather than examples: unknown never becomes absent, dry-run has no effect, a protected name resists every spelling.
CodeQL, Semgrep and SARIF parsing. Complements the repository's own codeql.yml by making the same analyses runnable locally during review.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust. Runs scanner binaries, which is code execution, so it carries the highest capability of the set and the largest always-on cost. Reconsider at the next review if it is not being used.

components.purpose: Dependency supply-chain risk. Serves ADR-0009 and docs/security/SUPPLY_CHAIN.md, and the dependency-ring rules of ADR-0019.
Checks code against the documents that specify it. This repository has 260 specifying documents and no mechanical link from a requirement to the code that implements it.

decision.rationale: Vendor trust; prompt and one subagent.

components.purpose: Language-server intelligence for the Rust workspace.

decision.rationale: First-party marketplace. Runs rust-analyzer, which the developer already runs.

rejected.reason: Duplicates project/*.json as a second source of truth for planning, without Change Risk Levels or safety gates. A second definition of Done in one repository is the class of defect the E00 review took three rounds to close.

Named personas passing context through files. The executor/verifier split here is stricter because it is bounded and because a CR4 verdict is not the executor's to write. Personas add theatre, not guarantees.
Duplicates scripts/project_os.py without the risk model or the gates.

Not rejected as worthless - four of its patterns were harvested into .claude/skills. Rejected as an installation, because it defines Done its own way and this repository already defines Done more strictly and ties it to safety invariants.

Rule 3 (surgical changes) was harvested into AGENTS.md's Diff discipline. The package is rejected: it is a CLAUDE.md, so it is always resident rather than progressively disclosed, and its rule 2 forbids 'error handling for unrealistic edge cases' - in this product the unrealistic edge cases are the product.
